headline: CBA's cash NPAT increased $730 million or 7.1% to $10,982 million in FY26 (ev-70). Total operating income grew 6.2% to $30,224 million, driven by a $1,563 million increase in NII and $196 million in other operating income (ev-47, ev-59, ev-1). Operating performance rose 6.5% to $16,469 million as underlying expenses grew 5.6% to $13,585 million and notable items were $170 million (ev-69, ev-68, ev-73). Loan impairment expense increased $62 million to $788 million, while corporate tax expense rose $208 million to $4,699 million (ev-27, ev-33). Statutory NPAT was $10,866 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $1,563 million or 7% on the prior year to $25,586 million (ev-59). This growth was supported by an 8% increase in average interest earning assets ($92 billion), partially offset by a 3 bps decrease in net interest margin to 2.05% (ev-57, ev-60, ev-58). The margin decline was driven by asset pricing (-5 bps) and funding costs, largely offset by volume growth and liquidity mix (ev-65, ev-66).

Other operating income increased $196 million or 4% to $4,638 million (ev-1). Commissions drove this with a $135 million increase to $2,234 million, lending fees rose $12 million to $924 million, funds management income grew $12 million to $134 million, and other income increased $46 million to $156 million (ev-2, ev-3, ev-5, ev-6). Trading income decreased slightly by $9 million to $1,190 million (ev-4).

Underlying operating expenses increased $719 million or 5.6% to $13,585 million (ev-68). Staff expenses rose 4% to $8,258 million, occupancy fell 2% to $938 million, IT services increased 16% to $2,782 million, and other expenses grew 4% to $1,607 million (ev-12, ev-13, ev-14, ev-15). Growth was driven by inflation, technology investment, and frontline/operations spending (ev-95).

Restructuring and notable items increased by $40 million to $170 million in FY26, compared to $130 million in FY25 (ev-17). This represents an additional negative contribution to earnings of $40 million year-on-year.

Loan impairment expense increased $62 million or 9% to $788 million (ev-27). The increase was primarily driven by Retail Banking Services (+$106 million to $378 million) and New Zealand (+$11 million to $66 million), partially offset by Business Banking (-$45 million to $310 million) and Institutional Banking (-$16 million to $33 million) (ev-28, ev-29, ev-23, ev-24, ev-25).

Corporate tax expense increased $208 million or 5% to $4,699 million (ev-33). This reflects a 30.0% effective tax rate, down 50 basis points from 30.5% in FY25, primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses (ev-34).

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items: $170 million in FY26 vs $130 million in FY25.
limitations: Capped at 80: operating_expenses -719 $m, notable_items -40 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
